+from typing import Optional
+
+
+def split_front_matter(text: str) -> tuple[Optional[str], str]:
+    """Split front matter separated by '---' delimiters.
+
+    Returns (front_matter_str, content_str), or (None, text) if no front matter
+    exists. Raises ValueError when the opening '---' delimiter is present but never
+    closed.
+    """
+    if not text.startswith("---"):
+        return (None, text)
+
+    # Check if the opening '---' is followed by a newline (or is the exact line)
+    # SlatePress front matter typically starts at index 0 on its own line.
+    # Let's find all lines or search for the closing delimiter.
+    # A valid opening delimiter line is '---' possibly followed by whitespace/newline.
+    # Let's inspect the first few characters:
+    # If text starts with '---', check if it's followed by a newline or space/tab then newline.
+    first_newline = text.find("\n")
+    if first_newline == -1:
+        # Just "---" with no newline and no content
+        # An opening delimiter must be on its own line. If text is just "---", it's unclosed.
+        if text.strip() == "---":
+            raise ValueError("Unclosed front matter delimiter")
+        return (None, text)
+
+    first_line = text[:first_newline].rstrip("\r")
+    if first_line != "---":
+        return (None, text)
+
+    # Search for the closing '---' delimiter on its own line after the first newline
+    # A closing delimiter is '---' at the start of a line (after newline), optionally followed by whitespace/newline.
+    pos = first_newline + 1
+    while True:
+        # Find next occurrence of '---'
+        next_dash = text.find("---", pos)
+        if next_dash == -1:
+            raise ValueError("Unclosed front matter delimiter")
+
+        # Verify this '---' is at the start of a line (preceded by a newline)
+        # and followed by a newline or end of string (possibly with trailing whitespace on the line).
+        is_start_of_line = (next_dash == 0 or text[next_dash - 1] == "\n")
+        if is_start_of_line:
+            # Check what follows '---' on that line
+            end_of_line = text.find("\n", next_dash)
+            if end_of_line == -1:
+                line_remainder = text[next_dash:]
+            else:
+                line_remainder = text[next_dash:end_of_line]
+
+            cleaned_remainder = line_remainder.rstrip("\r")
+            if cleaned_remainder == "---":
+                # Found the closing delimiter!
+                front_matter_str = text[first_newline + 1:next_dash]
+                # Strip leading newline from content if present
+                content_start = end_of_line if end_of_line != -1 else len(text)
+                if content_start < len(text) and text[content_start] == "\n":
+                    content_start += 1
+                elif content_start + 1 < len(text) and text[content_start:content_start+2] == "\r\n":
+                    content_start += 2
+                
+                content_str = text[content_start:]
+                return (front_matter_str, content_str)
+
+        pos = next_dash + 3
+
+
+def parse_front_matter(text: str) -> dict[str, str]:
+    """Parse front matter text into a dictionary of key-value pairs.
+
+    Supports simple 'key: value' lines and ignores comment lines beginning with '#'.
+    Whitespace around keys and values is stripped.
+    """
+    result: dict[str, str] = {}
+    if not text:
+        return result
+
+    lines = text.splitlines()
+    for line in lines:
+        stripped = line.strip()
+        if not stripped or stripped.startswith("#"):
+            continue
+
+        # Split on the first colon ':'
+        parts = stripped.split(":", 1)
+        if len(parts) == 2:
+            key = parts[0].strip()
+            val = parts[1].strip()
+            if key:
+                result[key] = val
+
+    return result
